definition: In learning research, a terminal link is the later part of a choice sequence in which a selected option leads to a signal that indicates the chance of reinforcement or nonreinforcement. Its value can strongly influence preference, sometimes more than the overall frequency of reward.

reasons: The packet does not explicitly define a “terminal link” as the “later part of a choice sequence”; it only refers to a “terminal link stimulus value” in explaining pigeons’ suboptimal choice behavior.
Because the term’s structural definition (“later part of a choice sequence”) is not stated in the packet, the requested sense is not fully supported.
The packet supports a ‘terminal link stimulus value’ account in pigeons, but it does not define ‘terminal link’ itself as the later part of a choice sequence that leads to a signal.

The phrasing about a signal indicating the chance of reinforcement or nonreinforcement is only partly supported; the packet discusses stimuli predicting reinforcement probabilities, not a general definition of terminal links.

The claim that this term’s value can influence preference more than overall reward frequency goes beyond the packet’s wording and turns a specific experimental result into a broader definitional statement.
